CONCEPT, RULES & SOURCES

An operational resource game.

The concept comes from the supplied October 19, 2026 Melinda Yormick meeting notes and five CLARA slides: connected people, equipment, rooms and event dependencies. The Gemini notes may contain transcription errors. This game does not validate the deck’s clinical, prediction or savings claims.

Neurosurgery context

ZEISS describes neurosurgical microscopes, and Medtronic describes neurosurgical navigation. These sources ground equipment categories only. They do not support this game’s requirements, staffing levels, prices or case durations.

Fictional rules

  • Six scheduled cases: A/OR1 08:10, B/OR2 08:30, C/OR3 08:50, D/OR1 10:10, E/OR2 10:30, F/OR3 10:50. Default cranial cases take 90 minutes; spine cases 75. Type and duration are editable.
  • Default types each require one S, N, A and T. Cranial cases require ultrasound, microscope and navigation; spine cases require a microscope. These lists are incomplete, invented software gates and must not guide clinical staffing.
  • Staff and equipment are pooled across ORs. A case reserves all requirements together, no earlier than two minutes before its scheduled start. Resources walk or travel for two minutes and must arrive before the case starts. Allocation scans cases in planned order, skipping blocked cases that cannot reserve a complete set.
  • Room turnover is 15 minutes. Staff are unavailable for 10 minutes after a case: surgeons and scrub staff return to work spaces; nurses stay 8 minutes, then walk 2; anesthesia staff walk to recovery, stay 3 minutes, then walk to the lounge. Patient transfers are instantaneous and recovery lasts 30 minutes with unlimited capacity.
  • Equipment is exclusive. Ultrasound is released after the first 15 minutes; other units stay through case end. Each release takes 3 minutes cleaning and 2 minutes back to the hub. A subsequent dispatch takes another 2 minutes. Extra hold extends case A and its ultrasound use.
  • Illustrative hourly pay: S $180, N $55, A $130, T $45. Purchase/upkeep per operating day: US $60,000/$20; MC $450,000/$80; NV $250,000/$50. No market prices or employment costs are claimed. Pay accrues through the full 8-hour duty day, regardless of utilization; equipment maintenance accrues linearly. Daily purchase allocation uses 1,250 operating days. Full-purchase mode charges all owned units at time zero.
  • Default delay penalty: $25 per case-minute of late start, accumulating even if a case never starts. A $10,000 game penalty applies to each case not finished by 16:00. It does not represent death, harm, the value of a life, or any medical outcome.
  • Goal: all six cases completed by 16:00 with zero start delay, then lowest cost among setups you have tried with the same rules. Changing requirements creates a different challenge. No automatic staffing recommendation or proof of optimality is provided.
  • Everything is deterministic. Playing, stepping, rewinding and full-day runs replay identical event rules. The last 10 scored runs and current setup are stored only in this browser. CLARA prediction remains disabled.
